top.title: Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed champion
top.description: Lauren Price hopes to fight on bigger stages as her career continues [Getty Images] Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion. Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles. Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing. But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come. Price v Kotaskova: Watch undisputed title fight after Edwards v McGregor History, hunger and headline bills - why Price is box office Edwards' world title aim to join Welsh boxing greats Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity. Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness. Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise. The Tokyo gold medal winner could celebrate even before the final bell sounded, climbing the corner ropes and into the record books. It was lapped up by a sell-out Utilita Arena crowd who excitedly acknowledged the achievement and the moment. Wales has produced 14 world champions, some of them genuine greats. They include, of course, Joe Calzaghe who so often graced this venue with successful defence after successful defence of his super-middleweight crown. He never reached undisputed status, though he was able to cross the capital city to go from arena to stadium champion. That is the next challenge for Price, claiming before she left the ring that more is to come while talk immediately turned to five-weight world champion Claressa Shields as a stadium fight next summer. Champions recognise champions That is for the future, but this was a night for history - with the calibre of some of the former boxers in the stands a nod to that. Champions know champions. Five Welsh world title winners were in the capital to watch their compatriot do something never been done before. From Cinderella Man Steve Robinson and Barry Jones, to the more recent Joe Cordina, who may still be eyeing a stadium return of his own in the coming weeks. All have been proud to fly the flag, but perhaps none have worn it quite as much on their sleeve - or shorts - as Price has done. top.title: Newport not taking anything for granted - Mullins
top.description: [Huw Evans Picture Agency] On this day a year ago, Christian Fuchs was appointed Newport County head coach , but now under another former Premier League player, Newport continue to make significant strides forwards – albeit with a much stronger and experienced squad. Newport County's progress under Hayden Mullins has been clear to see, but the Exiles boss was keen to stress that his side will not get carried away. County welcome Swindon Town to Rodney Parade on Saturday, 21 November (12:30 GMT) looking to extend their unbeaten home league record, having already collected 15 points on home soil, just seven shy of the 22 County managed across the entirety of the last campaign. While their away form remains a work in progress, Newport continue to climb the League Two table and earned a credible point at play-off hopefuls Crewe Alexandra last weekend despite leading 2-0. "The boys have done really well," said Mullins. "They have gone into games where people would have given us no chance [and picked up points]. "No one would have said we'd be 2-0 up at half-time on Saturday and potentially could have won the game, so it was a good performance to come out with a draw away from home. "We've been really unlucky not to pick up the results I felt we've deserved. In certain moments in games our performances have let us down and we need to address that to give us the opportunity to be a little bit higher." Having already beaten Swindon 2-0 in the EFL Trophy this season confidence within the squad is growing, but Mullins insists Newport must remain focused. "We're not taking anything for granted," he added. "We want to work hard, take every game as it comes, not look past any games and make sure we're set up in the right way for every game." That mindset is shared by defender Dan Sassi, who, though Newport have just one win in their last five league games feels Newport should not fear anybody. "We fancy ourselves against anyone in this league," said Sassi. "We've got some great talent in the group and the spirit is amazing. We're taking it game by game, but we're definitely looking upwards." For a club that spent much of last season looking over its shoulder, that growing sense of looking upwards is perhaps just the relief they craved.

top.description: Four weeks ago, Rutgers took a set off Michigan State at Jersey Mike’s Arena, 28-26, in a four-set loss that at least had an argument in it. In the first Big Ten Tournament match in program history, they did not reach 17 points in any of three sets. Michigan State swept Rutgers 25-16, 25-15, 25-13 on Friday at Fishers Event Center in Fishers, Ind., in the first round of the inaugural Big Ten Tournament, a match that was over in 81 minutes in front of an announced 6,866. The No. 11 seed Spartans move on to No. 6 Minnesota on Saturday. The No. 14 seed Scarlet Knights go home, and the season is over. Michigan State hit .415 with 48 kills and nine attack errors on 94 swings. Rutgers hit .065 with 25 kills and 19 errors on 92. The Spartans out-blocked Rutgers 12-3, out-aced them 5-2, out-dug them 42-28 and sided out at 68.9 percent against Rutgers’ 40.5. Rutgers’ best set was the one they hit .129 in, and they lost that one 25-13. The worst part is that Rutgers was level or ahead in all three sets, at 5-5 in the first, 11-9 in the second and 6-4 in the third. From those three scores to the end of each set, Michigan State outscored them 57-22. That is about as bad as an 11-versus-14 matchup gets. top.title: How Does Royce Lewis Fit On Dodgers After Reported Trade?
top.description: Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis The Los Angeles Dodgers have reportedly acquired Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for Bobby Miller and Francisco Espinoza, according to FanSided's Robert Murray . Lewis was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 MLB Draft and looked like a star in the making after he made his debut in 2022. However, he has failed to live up to high expectations and has been held back by countless injuries. Miller was once the No. 2 prospect in the Dodgers organization, so it's essentially a trade of great prospects who may need a change of scenery after failing to live up to the hype. Lewis is a versatile defender and could be used in a utility role. The Dodgers are pretty much set when it comes to starters, but Lewis could fill the void left by Miguel Rojas retiring. The Dodgers have aging veterans Mookie Betts, Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman who may need more days off moving forward. Lewis can play all of their positions, and the hope is that the Dodgers can unlock his full potential on offense. Lewis had a .307/.364/.549 slash line with 17 home runs in his first 70 games as a big leaguer. Since then, he does have 44 home runs, but an overall OPS of .689. There is pop in his bat, but he strikes out a ton. He is kind of an all-or-nothing type of hitter right now, but that could change with the proper coaching. He was a non-tender candidate, but the Dodgers clearly liked him enough to trade for him. More MLB: Reds Slugger Wins 2026 NL Rookie Of The Year

top.title: Diamondbacks non-tender Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston
top.description: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 05: Relief pitcher Andrew Saalfrank #27 of the Arizona Diamondbacks pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the eighth inning at Chase Field on September 05, 2025 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Diamondbacks defeated the Red Sox 10-5. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today was the the deadline for teams to decide on whether or not to offer contracts to the players in their arbitration seasons and below. The D-backs did so for just about everyone on their list, but there were a couple of notable exceptions. Of the players on the Arizona roster eligible for arbitration, they made the (largely no brainer) decisions to extend contracts to all three: C Gabriel Moreno, RHP Ryne Nelson and OF Lars Nootbaar. However, two other pre-arbitration players, both left-handed pitchers – Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston were non-tendered, and so have now become free agents. Saalfrank is perhaps the better known of the pair, for reasons both good and bad. The then 26-year-old exploded onto the team late in the 2023 season, not allowing an earned run in his first ten appearances in the major-leagues. That got him a spot on the D-backs post-season roster that year, and he added four more scoreless outings in the Wild Card and Divisional Series, before giving up a run Game 3 + 4 of the NLCS. He got a blown save in the former, although the D-backs won. He finished the playoffs with a 3.18 ERA across 11 post-season games, and was expected to be a big part of the Arizona bullpen for 2024. He didn’t make the Opening Day roster and, after being called up in April, a disastrous outing in Los Angeles got him quickly optioned back to Reno. Worse was to come: in June, word came that he had been found guilty of gambling on baseball. There’s no indication he ever bet on himself, and he was by all accounts quite terrible. But a year’s suspension was mandatory, derailing him entirely. Saalfrank returned the following year, and pitched very well down the stretch (a 1.24 ERA across 29 innings). But this February he had shoulder surgery to remove bone spurs and perform a labrum repair. He never made it back to the mound and it appears his time with the team is now over. Walston only made nine appearances at the major-league level, the first coming back in May 2024. However, he had Tommy John surgery in early 2025, which cost him the entire season and then some. He only returned to the minor-leagues in August this year. Though Blake did get a cup of coffee in September with the big-league club, allowing a run over three innings. But, again, it seems the D-backs had no further use for him. With both players being pre-arbitration, their departures won’t move the needle much with regard to payroll. However, they do open up two more spots on the roster, which is at 31, not including the potential arrival of Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox.

top.title: Giants ink former All-Star closer to $6.3 million contract
top.description: The San Francisco Giants are coming off a dreadful 2026 season. There were holes throughout the roster, but one that might have been shored up to some degree on Friday with the news that the Giants came to terms with relief pitcher Camilo Doval on a one-year, $6.3 million contract, per The Athletic. Doval’s journey brought him back to the San Francisco Giants late in 2026 and he’ll remain there for at least 2027. The 29-year-old right-hander was claimed by the Giants off waivers from the Pittsburgh Pirates in late September after San Francisco traded him to the New York Yankees ahead of the trade deadline in 2025. Camilo Doval throws a pitch for the New York Yankees during a game against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on Wednesday, March 25, 2026. Charles Wenzelberg/New York Post It was a full circle moment for Doval, who signed with the Giants as an amateur free agent in 2015 as an 18-year-old. He made the All-Star team once in 2023 when he led MLB with 39 saves while striking out 87 hitters in 67 2/3 innings. Next season would be his seventh with the team. The Yankees acquired Doval to bolster their bullpen by sending four prospects back to the Giants in 2025. Doval appeared in 22 regular season games and three playoffs contests for New York, who lost in the Divisional Series to the Toronto Blue Jays in four games. San Francisco Giants pitcher Camilo Doval (75) pitches against the Miami Marlins in the ninth inning at Oracle Park in San Francisco on Friday, April 8, 2022. USA TODAY Sports The Giants initially traded Doval during a strong season in 2025 when he had a 3.09 ERA in 47 games. His ERA jumped to 4.82 over the remainder of the season with New York, who traded him to Pittsburgh for a pair of prospects Aug. 1. top.title: Capitalizing on motion and play-action inside the Jaguars offense
top.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hands the ball to Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Johnnie Izquierdo The Jaguars’ offense has been exceptional this season. That’s not really a secret. Seemingly anything and everything Liam Coen implements strikes gold. Among those things is the Jaguars’ success with motion, play under-center, and with play-action. In 2026, Trevor Lawrence is seeing career-highs in use of motion (75.2%), play under-center (45.7%), and play-action (26.8%). The Jaguars just so happen to be about the best team in the NFL in all three departments. Jacksonville’s use of motion over the years is a confusing one. Former head coach Doug Pederson stayed pretty consistent in his use of motion, despite the league seeing a dramatic uptick. In 2024, his final season in Jacksonville, the Jaguars ranked 31st at just 47.9%. Since then, Liam Coen has nearly doubled that figure in two seasons. The Jags are now seeing pre-snap motion on 75% of snaps, the fourth-highest mark in the league. As a whole, the team ranks third in yards per game (281.3), third in yards per play (6.2), and second in EPA per play with motion. It’s no surprise then to see Lawrence has the second-most passing yards in the league with 1,613 yards. On the ground, the Jags rank sixth in yards (873) when utilizing motion. From under-center, Trevor Lawrence is completing 73.3% of his passes for 665 yards, six touchdowns, zero interceptions, and an NFL-best 142.7 passer rating. His 11.08 yards per attempt, 73.3% completion rate, 63.3% success rate, and +0.59 EPA per play all rank either first or second in the NFL. The Jags’ ability to run the ball from under-center certainly helps the cause. Bhayshul Tuten ranks fifth in the NFL with 509 yards gained from under-center, according to Fantasy Points. It’s that success that makes the Jaguars’ use of play-action so deadly, a new tool at Trevor Lawrence’s disposal. When using play-action, Lawrence has completed 72% of his passes for 797 yards, six touchdowns and zero interceptions, and another NFL-best passer rating of 133.0. He again is Top-2 in yards per attempt (10.6), success rate (64%), and EPA per play (+0.552). It’s this marriage of coaching and talent between Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence that has made this Jaguars’ offense so scary. Yes, Trevor Lawrence is playing the best football of his career and maybe in the entire NFL. top.title: Dustin May’s Four Rings Prove Baseball’s New Reality
top.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May (21) pitches during the first inning against the Tampa Bay Rays during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026. Dustin May has four World Series rings, and that number is now shared only with Mookie Betts among active players. The former Dodgers pitcher reached this milestone after helping the Milwaukee Brewers eliminate Los Angeles in the 2026 National League Championship Series. “It’s crazy to fathom that I have four rings,” May said. “It’s kind of something that not many people in this world have ever accomplished and it’s crazy to even think that my name is attached to that.” The Road Was Not Smooth May’s path to the fourth ring was filled with physical pain and unexpected twists. He sat out the full 2024 campaign while healing a torn flexor tendon located in his right arm. An esophageal tear resulting from a freak accident involving a salad required surgery, making things worse. Despite missing time, he still earned a championship ring for the 2024 campaign. Once he resumed playing as a workhorse for the Dodgers during 2025, the Boston Red Sox acquired him at the deadline. He was credited with another ring that season despite leaving the team early. Money Follows The Wins A winning performance with Milwaukee during the second half of the 2026 season probably increased his market value this winter. After securing a three-year, $52.5 million contract in free agency, May now is a pitcher for the Chicago White Sox. This contract shows that teams still pay big for proven winners, even when their recent history includes major injuries. The Cost Of The Spotlight While May celebrates, other players struggle with the pressure that comes with winning and losing. Walker Kessler, who plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, recently discussed how scrutiny can ruin the joy of sports. He noted that some players enter the league loving the game but get blinded by the extra noise. “So they lose the love of the game because they focus so much on all the other stuff, and it’s sad to see,” Kessler said on The Old Man and the Three podcast. May seems to have avoided that trap, keeping his focus on the work rather than the noise. His four rings stand as proof that the game can still be enjoyed if the player stays true to the grind.

(Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Michael Reaves/Getty Images NAPLES, Fla. — A Lim Kim pulled away from a crowded pack in a most spectacular fashion Friday when she made a hole-in-one on the par-3 16th hole and posted an 8-under 64 to build a three-shot lead over defending champion Jeeno Thitikul in the CME Group Tour Championship. It also helped that Kim picked up birdies on all four of the par 5s at Tiburon Golf Club. She finished with a long two-putt par to reach 15-under 129, the lowest 36-hole score since this tournament moved to Tiburon in 2013. Nelly Korda, in her bid to win the season finale to get into the LPGA Hall of Fame, shot a 67 and still wound up losing ground. She started three shots behind and now is six back on a course that has been relatively soft with wide fairways that allow for low scoring. Korda said she has been battling a two-way miss that she is still trying to figure out. “It gets frustrating because I feel like I have a thought and then I look at my swing and I’m like, ‘This is all timing and it’s just ...’ Yeah, golf is fun sometimes, right?” It certainly felt that way to Kim, the 2020 U.S. Women’s Open champion, who had a calm hand with the putter and delivered one shot that stole the spotlight on a warm, cloudy day. She hit 7-iron from 168 yards that pitched in front of the pin, took one bounced and disappeared. She stretched out both arms in a quiet, surprised celebration. Kim followed with a 5-foot birdie on the par-5 17th and is halfway home to $4 million prize, the richest payoff in women’s golf. “I needed 155-yard shot, honestly a little strong hit and I make it,” Kim said of her ace. “A little luck to me, yeah.” She still has a solid chasing pack behind her. He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision. According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations. Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations. He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office. On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges. He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. nigeria.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
nigeria.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. nigeria.title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
nigeria.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). He also described himself as the most transparent individual. “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” Bello said on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday. ﻿ When asked to respond to allegations of financial mismanagement while in government, the former governor urged people in doubt to go to the state and ask questions about how resources were managed. He said he pities those who call him a thief. The former governor also described himself as a man who was blessed by God and able to meet his needs and those of his family members. Bello, who has consistently denied wrongdoing, is facing multiple cases instituted by the anti-graft agency over alleged misappropriation of public funds during his eight-year tenure as governor of the state. The EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said in an interview with Channels Television in January 2026 that the commission had filed three cases against the former governor and fulfilled its mandate by investigating and prosecuting him. According to Olukoyede, the responsibility for determining Bello’s guilt rests with the judiciary. One of the cases involves a 16-count charge bordering on alleged criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving ₦110.4 billion. Bello, who was the governor from 2016 to 2024, is standing trial alongside two former state government officials. The Federal Government alleges that the defendants diverted state funds to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Bello is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2 billion fraud and money laundering before the Federal High Court in Abuja. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. sports.description: [Huw Evans Picture Agency] On this day a year ago, Christian Fuchs was appointed Newport County head coach , but now under another former Premier League player, Newport continue to make significant strides forwards – albeit with a much stronger and experienced squad. Newport County's progress under Hayden Mullins has been clear to see, but the Exiles boss was keen to stress that his side will not get carried away. County welcome Swindon Town to Rodney Parade on Saturday, 21 November (12:30 GMT) looking to extend their unbeaten home league record, having already collected 15 points on home soil, just seven shy of the 22 County managed across the entirety of the last campaign. While their away form remains a work in progress, Newport continue to climb the League Two table and earned a credible point at play-off hopefuls Crewe Alexandra last weekend despite leading 2-0. "The boys have done really well," said Mullins. "They have gone into games where people would have given us no chance [and picked up points]. "No one would have said we'd be 2-0 up at half-time on Saturday and potentially could have won the game, so it was a good performance to come out with a draw away from home. "We've been really unlucky not to pick up the results I felt we've deserved. In certain moments in games our performances have let us down and we need to address that to give us the opportunity to be a little bit higher." Having already beaten Swindon 2-0 in the EFL Trophy this season confidence within the squad is growing, but Mullins insists Newport must remain focused. "We're not taking anything for granted," he added. "We want to work hard, take every game as it comes, not look past any games and make sure we're set up in the right way for every game." That mindset is shared by defender Dan Sassi, who, though Newport have just one win in their last five league games feels Newport should not fear anybody. "We fancy ourselves against anyone in this league," said Sassi. "We've got some great talent in the group and the spirit is amazing. We're taking it game by game, but we're definitely looking upwards." The Diamondbacks defeated the Red Sox 10-5. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today was the the deadline for teams to decide on whether or not to offer contracts to the players in their arbitration seasons and below. The D-backs did so for just about everyone on their list, but there were a couple of notable exceptions. Of the players on the Arizona roster eligible for arbitration, they made the (largely no brainer) decisions to extend contracts to all three: C Gabriel Moreno, RHP Ryne Nelson and OF Lars Nootbaar. However, two other pre-arbitration players, both left-handed pitchers – Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston were non-tendered, and so have now become free agents. Saalfrank is perhaps the better known of the pair, for reasons both good and bad. The then 26-year-old exploded onto the team late in the 2023 season, not allowing an earned run in his first ten appearances in the major-leagues. That got him a spot on the D-backs post-season roster that year, and he added four more scoreless outings in the Wild Card and Divisional Series, before giving up a run Game 3 + 4 of the NLCS. He didn’t make the Opening Day roster and, after being called up in April, a disastrous outing in Los Angeles got him quickly optioned back to Reno. But a year’s suspension was mandatory, derailing him entirely. Saalfrank returned the following year, and pitched very well down the stretch (a 1.24 ERA across 29 innings). sports.title: Capitalizing on motion and play-action inside the Jaguars offense
sports.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hands the ball to Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Johnnie Izquierdo The Jaguars’ offense has been exceptional this season. That’s not really a secret. Seemingly anything and everything Liam Coen implements strikes gold. Among those things is the Jaguars’ success with motion, play under-center, and with play-action. In 2026, Trevor Lawrence is seeing career-highs in use of motion (75.2%), play under-center (45.7%), and play-action (26.8%). The Jaguars just so happen to be about the best team in the NFL in all three departments. Jacksonville’s use of motion over the years is a confusing one. Former head coach Doug Pederson stayed pretty consistent in his use of motion, despite the league seeing a dramatic uptick. In 2024, his final season in Jacksonville, the Jaguars ranked 31st at just 47.9%. Since then, Liam Coen has nearly doubled that figure in two seasons. The Jags are now seeing pre-snap motion on 75% of snaps, the fourth-highest mark in the league. As a whole, the team ranks third in yards per game (281.3), third in yards per play (6.2), and second in EPA per play with motion. It’s no surprise then to see Lawrence has the second-most passing yards in the league with 1,613 yards. On the ground, the Jags rank sixth in yards (873) when utilizing motion. From under-center, Trevor Lawrence is completing 73.3% of his passes for 665 yards, six touchdowns, zero interceptions, and an NFL-best 142.7 passer rating. His 11.08 yards per attempt, 73.3% completion rate, 63.3% success rate, and +0.59 EPA per play all rank either first or second in the NFL. The Jags’ ability to run the ball from under-center certainly helps the cause. Bhayshul Tuten ranks fifth in the NFL with 509 yards gained from under-center, according to Fantasy Points. It’s that success that makes the Jaguars’ use of play-action so deadly, a new tool at Trevor Lawrence’s disposal. When using play-action, Lawrence has completed 72% of his passes for 797 yards, six touchdowns and zero interceptions, and another NFL-best passer rating of 133.0. He again is Top-2 in yards per attempt (10.6), success rate (64%), and EPA per play (+0.552). It’s this marriage of coaching and talent between Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence that has made this Jaguars’ offense so scary. Yes, Trevor Lawrence is playing the best football of his career and maybe in the entire NFL. An esophageal tear resulting from a freak accident involving a salad required surgery, making things worse. Despite missing time, he still earned a championship ring for the 2024 campaign. Once he resumed playing as a workhorse for the Dodgers during 2025, the Boston Red Sox acquired him at the deadline. He was credited with another ring that season despite leaving the team early. Money Follows The Wins A winning performance with Milwaukee during the second half of the 2026 season probably increased his market value this winter. After securing a three-year, $52.5 million contract in free agency, May now is a pitcher for the Chicago White Sox. This contract shows that teams still pay big for proven winners, even when their recent history includes major injuries. The Cost Of The Spotlight While May celebrates, other players struggle with the pressure that comes with winning and losing. Walker Kessler, who plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, recently discussed how scrutiny can ruin the joy of sports. He noted that some players enter the league loving the game but get blinded by the extra noise. “So they lose the love of the game because they focus so much on all the other stuff, and it’s sad to see,” Kessler said on The Old Man and the Three podcast. May seems to have avoided that trap, keeping his focus on the work rather than the noise. His four rings stand as proof that the game can still be enjoyed if the player stays true to the grind.

technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

technology.description: Each generation of Intel Xeons or AMD Epycs brings dozens of new SKUs: high-core count parts tuned for throughput, high-frequency ones optimized for latency, low-power chips designed for the edge, and everything in between. But if you ask Ian Finder, who heads development of Nvidia’s datacenter CPUs, for the vast majority of use cases, all those SKUs are overkill. “There was sort of an overskewing, for many years on the other vendors side of things,” he told El Reg on the sidelines of Supercomputing 2026 this week. Nvidia is a relative newcomer to the datacenter CPU space. The company’s first part, called Grace, launched in 2023, but didn’t see widespread deployment outside AI headnodes, high-end NICs, and a handful of standalone CPU deployments by hyperscalers like Meta. We explored the chip in greater detail earlier this year, but the GPU slinger’s latest CPU, Vera, is a different beast. In addition to showing up as part of Nvidia’s Vera-Rubin superchips, the CPU will also be offered in standalone CPU racks, storage, and context memory systems. Just this week, Nvidia announced a new rack with 192 Vera CPUs aimed at high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, which don’t translate well to GPUs. And at least on paper, a single SKU with 88 cores clocking to 3.3 GHz powers all of them. Historically, CPUs with different combinations of cores, clocks, I/O, and power have been used in these roles. According to Finder, most datacenter CPUs haven’t been loaded that heavily, and as a result unloaded latency has been the optimization point. As a consequence, CPUs that rely on high core counts to boost throughput often suffer from elevated loaded latencies. On the flip side, chipmakers can optimize for loaded latency, but this usually comes at the expense of throughput. We see this pretty clearly across AMD’s last few generations of Epycs, where it designed both space-efficient Zen-C cores that prioritize throughput and fatter frequency-optimized versions that prioritize latency. “As more cores are up and running, your latency to memory gets higher because you have to deal with congestion on the connectivity buses,” More than Moore analyst Ian Cutress tells The Reg . “What Nvidia is saying is right. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. science.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. That's where an eclipse almost 1,300 years later becomes particularly intriguing. Is the oldest recorded eclipse hidden in the Bible? Researchers have proposed that an annular eclipse occurred over Canaan on Oct. 30, 1207 BC, and may be described in the Bible. This image was captured during an annular solar eclipse from Redding, California on May 20, 2012. (Image credit: Paul Souders via Getty Images) A passage in the Old Testament book of Joshua describes the sun and moon as if they stopped in the sky. In research published in 2017, researchers Colin Humphreys and Graeme Waddington at Cambridge University in the U.K. claimed it could refer to an annular solar eclipse on Oct. 30, 1207 B.C. science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. Physical or cyberattacks against ground sites and other terrestrial infrastructure supporting space operations can also threaten satellite services. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Read more OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published a statement today claiming to have solved the problem with the aid of Anthropic’s Claude AI. Advertisement “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” writes Alpöge. “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” In August, Anthropic announced previous work on the Riemann hypothesis , but that stopped short of a full proof. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.

science.title: I got to tour SpaceX's Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, and what I saw blew my mind
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless. The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies. For some context, the five-story-tall Starfactory spans approximately 1 million square feet (~93,000 meters), with operations split between Starship's Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, and nearly 330,000 additional square feet (30,000 square meters) of office space. SpaceX officials describe its design as one more akin to an automotive manufacturing plant than that of a typical aerospace production site, and inside, it is absolutely alive with activity. Inside Starfactory We entered through an arch-covered doorway underneath the giant "X" sign on the building's shorter face. Our media gaggle was met with curious glances as we were shown through the doors and guided onto the factory floor - few are ever able to cross that threshold outside of SpaceX employees, and our presence seemed as novel to those busy working as it was to us. Inside, we were struck with the sheer enormity of Starship's scale. Giant stainless-steel rocket parts were meticulously scattered across different subassembly stations throughout the building, with Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections and booster components all under various stages of manufacture. The sheer quantity of the hardware was staggering, and being so close to each as we walked Starfactory's throughways was an eye-opener. The exterior of SpaceX's Starfactory facility at Starbase, Texas. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Future) Starbase is a unique partnership of privately-owned SpaceX property and publicly-accessible land and shoreline, which has created the unique ability for anyone with a mind to do so to drive right up to the the Starship launch pad to see the facilities up close (within a few hundred feet or so, which, as rockets go, is very, very close). Fully stacked, Starship stands more than 400 feet (120 meters) tall. Standing next to such a towering colossus on the pad is enough to drive home just how big the launch vehicle is, but standing next its segmented components inside Starfactory is even more humbling; like seeing one of Ship's upper aerodynamic flaps, which are each large enough when laid flat that you could park a pair of large SUVs on their faces with room to spare.
